name: Philippines (First Republic, 1898–1901)
description: Horizontal stripes of blue over red with a white equilateral triangle at the hoist bearing a golden sun with eight rays and a face, and a yellow five-pointed star in each corner of the triangle.
history: The flag first displayed at the Battle of Alapan on 28 May 1898 and formally unfurled at the proclamation of Philippine independence in Kawit on 12 June 1898, sewn in Hong Kong for Emilio Aguinaldo. In this original form the sun bore a mythological face. It was the flag of the First Philippine Republic until Aguinaldo's capture in 1901, and public display was banned by the American authorities from 1907 to 1919.
